title: Tommy Dorsey's playing and Glenn Miller's In the Mood
summary: He heard Dorsey play like no one but himself; they argue Joe Garland made Glenn Miller famous with In the Mood.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you ever hear Tommy Dorsey playing his stuff, that you feel he took from you?
The ideas that came from you.
I haven't heard him play like nobody but himself.
You know what made Glenn Miller famous?
Miller, and that's why I love him.
Did you ever know what made Glenn Miller famous?
Joe Garland made Glenn Miller famous, with In the Mood.

Joe Garland wrote it; Edgar Hayes played it. Edgar Hayes was the first musician - you know Edgar Hayes; he's my girl friend's husband. They live out in California. We all came up together. Edgar Hayes wanted to buy that music. When I lived down on ( ) Seventh Avenue he lived down there too, he and his wife. They all wanted to buy this music. He wouldn't sell it to nobody but Glenn Miller, Joe Garland.
He didn't sell it to Glenn Miller. Joe Garland is rich off of that tune today.
Edgar Hayes is the first one that ever recorded it.

Glenn Miller made the tune popular. That's Joe Garland's tune and Joe Garland is collecting the money and Joe Garland has got money like this and as long as he lives it's going to keep coming in every time he plays the record.
